questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I have heard good about the university of Valencia and the city in overall

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The beginning was a bit confusing with the matriculación

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I got everything important send on email and it was easy to follow all the steps

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a local student as a "buddy" that offered help if needed. I didn't need to use it though, but it was nice to know that someone at my own age was available

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult because I was maybe out a bit last minute. I found my place in October and had to start in February

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is important to search for something in good time to be able to live cheap and in a good location

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use it

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had a 2 week period of matriculación where we could change courses as we wanted. Afterwards, it was binding. I found it a bit confusing because I had to make sure that any of my classes overlapped. At the same time it was a good, because I had scheduled a course from home that I no-way was interested in attending. So it was good that I was able to change but at the same time it was a confusing process, because the courses also got full quickly and I had to choose some that I semi-wanted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much help. The secretary just informed about the procedure but we had to handle it ourselves

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I made 3 out of 5 of those I expected to do from home

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Knowing that there's a big chance of changing some of the courses you plan from home - either because the course doesn't turn out as expected, the level is too high or you simply find another one more interesting. So be prepared to change and go through all the "forhåndsgodkendelse" etc. again

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was really different from course to course. I had one course that was super easy that didn't took much effort to pass. On the other hand, I had 3 other courses that was really difficult to pass. All the teachers demanded a lot. So despite they represented the same credits, the level and work load was really different

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is really different. In UCPH it's way more self-studying and the responsibility to succeed is on your own. Here, the system is more like highschool in Denmark with tasks during the course that you have to hand in or tests. In some of my classes, the teacher also took notes of the absence / presence that had an influence in the final evaluation

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Spanish and languages of the Hispanic world (35518)
American Spanish (35517)
Norms and correct usage of Spanish (35660)
Lecturas contemporáneas hispanoamericanas (35530)
Expresión oral y escrita en el español académico y profesional (35538)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked "American Spanish". The teacher was really good and I learned a lot from there. 
"Lecturas contemporáneas hispanoamericanas" was also really interesting but way more demanding. We had to read 3 books during the semester + hand in 2 comments about a short story and do tests.

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I subscriped to a bike-company that has bikes all over the city. I didn't use the public transport too much but the bike was really useful. 
Besides that I subscriped to a gym also. I did not spend anything on books for uni, since everything was available online

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The rent but I was also out in last minute and I prioritized to live as central as possible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of sports-offerings that you could subscripe to for a little amount

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports offerings. I did not attend to any myself, but I heard from a lot down here that it was great (fx the surf school that the uni had a collab with)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to the other cities around. I went a lot to the coastline between Valencia and Alicante and there are so many small, cute villages on the coastline. It is easy going there with either train or bus and it's nice to come out of the city to a smaller more local environment

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy knowing some stuff from home. Fx that you write formally to your teacher on mail, but that the oral communication is pretty much like in Denmark. I expected a more formal environment in the class room but it was really casual

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak spanish and be open

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the local students a bit reserved and not that interested in interacting with erasmus-students. Maybe because there's so many in Valencia, I don't know. But for me, the university could do a bit more effort

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That the spanish people are really open and sweet. They are not reserved as some people in Denmark can appear. They like to talk and have an interest in you

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There's a lot of exchange students in Valencia. It takes an effort to get to know the locals 
2. Have patience in the beginning with the matriculation. It will be solved in the end 
3. Enjoy and try to go outside Valencia as well. There's so many beautiful places around

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Since the faculties are far apart, maybe it's the best to just choose courses from 1 faculty. I was supposed to take from different ones, but found it too confusing in the beginning so changed to only my own

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To try to live in Spain and experience the culture for more than just 2 weeks vacation. Get friendships from different european countries

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
To approach people I don't know and speak to a lot of new people. 
To adjust to a different uni-system and the work-load in the courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
